raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.12.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #5172

When numerics intentionally change, it's pretty annoying to regenerate new golden loss/grad norm, especially when you don't have the right hardware. This logs both expected / failing loss & norms on all steps when they fail.

Before:

```
[LOSS_COMPARE] Asserting loss values are equal...
FAIL: test_losses_equal (...)
AssertionError: 8.023916244506836 != 8.026254653930664 : loss mismatch at step 1: baseline=8.023916244506836, imported=8.026254653930664
[LOSS_COMPARE] loss assertion failed!
[LOSS_COMPARE] Actual baseline loss values (can be used to update the import file if the change is expected):
[LOSS_COMPARE] Note that you should verify the loss curve change is not a regression first!!!
1 8.023916244506836
2 7.69608211517334
...
10 4.052786350250244
```

After (the per-metric unittest failures for loss and grad_norm are printed
first, as before):

```
[LOSS_COMPARE] Metric mismatch. Full per-step values ('*' marks mismatching steps):
step  loss[baseline]      loss[imported]      grad_norm[baseline]  grad_norm[imported]
1 *   8.023916244506836   8.026254653930664   1.5995213985443115   1.5741771459579468
2 *   7.69608211517334    7.746360778808594   1.4733530282974243   1.4472531080245972
...
10 *  4.052786350250244   4.109261512756348   1.858564853668213    1.8730801343917847
[LOSS_COMPARE]
[LOSS_COMPARE] Baseline metrics in import file format (verify the change is not a regression before updating the import file):
# config: llama3_debugmodel_fsdp2_tp2_cp2
# ngpu: 8
# step loss grad_norm
1 8.023916244506836 1.5995213985443115
2 7.69608211517334 1.4733530282974243
...
10 4.052786350250244 1.858564853668213
```
